title: Mitigate heuristic-aging causing inference slowdown and p99 spikes
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:

Between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09 we observed recurrent throughput degradation and p99 latency spikes for several production inference routes running mixed-quant models. Symptoms appeared as gradual tail-latency drift across hosts followed by periodic cascades which temporarily reduced effective capacity by ~25% on impacted pools. The production alerting surfaced increased request queueing and degraded observed throughput per GPU.

Scope & Impact:
- Affected: hosted and dedicated pools serving medium-length chat workloads (seq_len 512–1024) on a mix of A100/RTX clusters.
- Customer-visible: intermittent p99 regressions (200–400ms increase) and timeout retries; elevated cost due to autoscale burst and fallbacks. Estimated customer-impact: medium.
- Surface area: scheduler kernel-ranking subsystem, runtime attention micro-optimizations, and prefix/KV cache eviction dynamics.

Hypothesis & Root Cause Summary:
We attribute the incident to "heuristic aging": the scheduler maintains statistical scoring for kernel candidates (latency/cost estimates) based on sliding windows of historical runs. A gradual shift in incoming request token distribution (more mid-length sequences and higher use of function-calling tokens) combined with a recent attention micro-optimization changed execution profiles for a subset of kernels. Over ~36 hours the scheduler's aging weights biased towards an emergent but suboptimal kernel ordering for several request shapes. This ordering interacted poorly with the KV cache eviction policy and microbatch packing, causing frequent micro-recompiles and cache thrashing that amplified tail latency.

Contributing factors:
- Aging window for kernel scores was too long and lacked freshness signals for fast workload shifts.
- Recent attention optimization (PR #7842) altered memory access patterns making one kernel variant more sensitive to microbatch size and KV cache warmth.
- Admission controls and batch-eviction heuristics had no cross-signal from the scheduler; eviction decisions occasionally evicted hot KV pages during transient kernel handoffs.
- We lacked a robust synthetic probe coverage for medium-sequence, function-call-heavy prompt shapes which delayed detection.

What we observed during investigation:
- Canary traces showed repeated recompile events and 12–18% extra memcpy time for affected kernels.
- Scheduler score drift correlated with a 6-hour window where traffic composition changed after a customer release.
- Forcing deterministic kernel ranking removed the cascade, confirming ranking instability as upstream cause.

Short-term mitigations applied (complete or in-progress):
- Rollback of the attention micro-optimization in canary (rolled back to 2026-03-09 09:40 UTC).
- Emergency throttle: temporarily lower probe rate for scheduler kernel probing and apply conservative hysteresis on score decay.
- Adjust KV cache eviction threshold to prefer retention during micro-recompile windows.
- Added a synthetic probe job that mirrors medium-length function-calling prompt shapes into the canary fleet to detect rank drift earlier.

Long-term remediation goals (this ticket):
- Hardening scheduler scoring against distribution shifts by introducing short-term freshness signals and adaptive decay.
- Make kernel probing idempotent and rate-limited with backoff tied to observed recompiles per host.
- Improve cross-subsystem signals so eviction policy consults scheduler probe state (prevent eviction during transient handoffs).
- Expand synthetic workload matrix in the regression harness to cover function-call heavy sequences and medium-length chats.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- No recurrence of p99 cascades in canary for two full business weeks under mirrored traffic.
- New scheduler scoring rollout behind feature flag with telemetry that proves reduced probe-induced recompiles by >=80%.
- Automated regression tests added to CI covering the identified shapes.
- Documentation and runbook updates completed (runbook contains mitigation steps and deciders).
